sentences.text: Then, Bitcoin ripped to  about $81,100, a 7% pump in the space of 12 hours.   Now, this wasn't necessarily just people rushing  in to buy.
A big part of that move was a classic   short squeeze.
That's when traders betting on a  drop are forced to buy back as the price rises,   pushing it even higher.
According to Coin Glass  data, around $950 million in positions were   liquidated, more than $560 million of it from  shorts.
So, the market had already taken a hit   before the results were final.
Which brings us to  the here and now.
At least as I make this video,   Bitcoin is continuing to trade just a smidge above  80K.
So, can we say it has definitely reclaimed   80K?
Well, not quite yet.
Bitcoin has pushed back  above this key level, but it hasn't yet proven   that it could hold that level as support through  a retest and a weekly close.
Since the 29th of   October, 80K has been the ceiling.
And as of right  now, we're merely poking through that ceiling.   A proper reclaim needs three things.
The first  is daily closes above 80K, ideally with a weekly   close to match.
The second is a successful retest,  meaning Bitcoin dips back to 80K or a little below   it and bounces, proving its support again.
The  third is the right fuel, meaning rising spot   volume and ETF inflows rather than just leverage  and a short squeeze.
And to be clear, leverage is   running fairly hot.
Open interest hit its highest  level since September on the 3rd of November with   annualized funding around 11%.
Funding is the  fee leveraged traders pay each other to hold   their positions.
And when it's that high, a lot  of them are leaning the same way.
Now, if 80k does   flip back to support, here's what we should look  for.
The first hurdle is at around 81.5K to 82K.   That's where the average cost basis of the US spot  ETF buyer is.
Then there's 85K, a zone that has   rejected Bitcoin four times this year.
Long-term  holders own about 4 million coins with cost basis   between 85K and 118K.
So, there is plenty of  break even selling overhead.
In the bullish case,   Bitcoin clears 85K.
That support gets worked  through and the 87K high would likely go quickly   after.
On the flip side, getting rejected at 80K  and sent back down to 75K would undo the whole   picture.
Never mind what happens if 75K fails to  hold.
So 80K is the line.
85K is the next possible   major test.
